Fit Dynamic Nelson-Siegel Model to Time Series of Yield Curves

Source: R/dns-model.r
fit_dns_model.Rd

Fits the DNS model to a time series of yield curves.

Usage

fit_dns_model(
  yield_data,
  n_days = 60,
  parallel = FALSE,
  lambda_constraint = "constrained",
  initial_lambda = 0.0609,
  show_progress = TRUE,
  date_order = c("input", "ascending", "descending"),
  drop_failed = TRUE,
  warm_start = TRUE,
  method = c("optim", "profile")
)

Arguments

yield_data

Data frame. The yield curve data with a 'Date' column and remaining columns containing yield values for different maturities, named by maturity in years.

n_days

Integer. Number of most recent dates to include in the fitting. The window is selected by date, so it does not depend on the row order of yield_data.

parallel

Logical. If TRUE, use parallel processing to speed up computation.

lambda_constraint

Character. How to handle the lambda parameter (fixed, constrained, free).

initial_lambda

Numeric. Initial value for lambda parameter.

show_progress

Logical. If TRUE, display a progress bar.

date_order

Character. Row order of the returned parameters and fitted_yields: "input" (the default) keeps the order the selected rows had in yield_data, so a most-recent-first frame yields a most-recent-first result; "ascending" and "descending" sort explicitly.

drop_failed

Logical. If TRUE (the default) dates whose cross-section could not be fitted are removed from the result. If FALSE they are kept with NA parameters.

warm_start

Logical. If TRUE (the default) each cross-section is initialised from the previous date's fitted lambda, walking forward in calendar time. Ignored when parallel = TRUE, where the fits are not ordered, and by method = "profile", which needs no start values.

Note that warm starting makes a date's fit depend on which other dates are in the panel: fitting a month-end series directly and fitting the daily series that contains it give slightly different parameters on the shared dates, because the chain of start values differs. Set warm_start = FALSE for cross-sections that are independent of the panel they arrived in.

method

Character. Passed to fit_ns_model: "optim" (the default) or "profile".

Value

A list containing:

  • parameters: Data frame with model parameters for each date, plus beta1_change, beta2_change and beta3_change.

  • fitted_yields: Matrix of fitted yield values, one column per maturity column of yield_data. Maturities that were missing on a given date are NA.

  • maturities: Vector of maturities in years.

  • success_rate: Percentage of successful model fits.

  • failures: Data frame of dates that could not be fitted, with the reason.

  • at_bound: Logical matrix, one row per retained date and one column per parameter, marking fits that came to rest on a bound. Those dates' factor decompositions are not identified.

Details

The factor change columns are first differences in calendar order (\(\beta(t) - \beta(t-1)\)) regardless of the row order of the output, so they can be fed directly to estimate_dns_dynamics.

Examples

data(treasury_yields)

# The 60 most recent curves. The window is chosen by date, so passing the
# panel in either row order selects the same dates.
dns_result <- fit_dns_model(treasury_yields, n_days = 60, show_progress = FALSE)
#> Warning: Parameters rest on a bound in some fits: lambda on 38 (of 60 dates). The factor decomposition is not identified on those dates; see the at_bound element of the result, widen lower_bounds/upper_bounds, or check the yield scale.
dns_result
#> Dynamic Nelson-Siegel fit
#>   60 curves, 2024-10-03 to 2024-12-31
#>   maturities         0.0833  0.2500  0.5000  1.0000  2.0000  3.0000  5.0000  7.0000 10.0000 20.0000 30.0000
#>   rmse              5.10 bp median, 8.04 bp worst
#>   lambda            0.5000 median
#>   success rate      100.0%
#>   at bound          lambda on 38 (see $at_bound)
summary(dns_result)
#> Dynamic Nelson-Siegel fit
#>   60 curves, 2024-10-03 to 2024-12-31, 100.0% fitted
#>

#> 
#> Fit error (basis points):

#> 3.54 5.10 6.89 8.04
